flawed_step: Step 5: The proof attempt infers that every positive odd edge cut has size at least 3. A cut consisting of one bridge is possible without the bridgeless hypothesis.
counterexample: Take three disjoint copies of K4, subdivide one edge in each copy with a new vertex u_i, and add a new vertex c adjacent to u_1,u_2,u_3. The resulting finite simple connected graph is 3-regular. Each edge cu_i is the sole edge leaving a five-vertex lobe, so every perfect matching would have to contain all three edges cu_i, which is impossible because they share c.
assessment_summary:
1. Let G be a connected 3-regular graph. The handshake identity 3|V(G)|=2|E(G)| shows that |V(G)| is even. Justified: the right side is even.
2. Attempt to verify Tutte’s condition. For S=∅, G has no odd component because it is connected and has even order; now fix nonempty S and let C be an odd component of G−S. Justified: this handles the empty-set case separately.
3. The cut δ(C) satisfies 3|V(C)|=2|E(C)|+|δ(C)|, so |δ(C)| is odd. Justified: sum the degrees of vertices in C.
4. Connectivity of G implies |δ(C)|≥1. Justified: otherwise C would also be a component of G, although S is nonempty.
5. The attempted Petersen-style proof claims that, since |δ(C)| is positive and odd, |δ(C)|≥3. Not justified: |δ(C)| may equal 1 when its unique edge is a bridge.
6. If q is the number of odd components of G−S, the attempt therefore asserts that at least 3q edges join those components to S. Not justified: it relies on the false assertion in Step 5.
7. At most 3|S| edges leave S. Justified: every vertex of S has degree 3.
8. Combining Steps 6 and 7 would give 3q≤3|S| and hence q≤|S|. Not justified in the argument: the required lower bound from Step 6 was not established.
9. Tutte’s criterion would then give a perfect matching. Not justified here: the criterion’s inequality has not been proved for every S.
10. To determine whether this is merely a proof gap, take three disjoint copies of K4 and, in each, subdivide one edge by a new vertex u_i. Justified: each resulting lobe is finite and simple, has five vertices, u_i has degree 2, and every other vertex has degree 3.
11. Add a new vertex c and the three edges cu_1,cu_2,cu_3. Justified: this is a well-defined finite simple graph.
12. The resulting graph H is connected and 3-regular. Justified: c and every u_i now have degree 3, all other degrees remain 3, and c connects the three lobes.
13. Each lobe has five vertices and its only edge to the rest of H is cu_i. Justified: this follows directly from the construction.
14. Any perfect matching of H would have to contain every cu_i. Justified: omitting cu_i would require covering all five vertices of its lobe using internal matching edges, which is impossible because matching edges cover vertices in pairs.
15. No matching can contain cu_1,cu_2,cu_3 simultaneously because all three meet c; hence H has no perfect matching. Justified: a matching cannot contain two edges sharing a vertex. Thus the proposed statement is false, and the bridgeless hypothesis cannot be dropped.
